key_insight: A brief weekly online memory test, analyzed with a computational model, can generate a stable personalized score that tracks memory dysfunction over time.
clinical_relevance: This approach could enable scalable remote screening and longitudinal monitoring of early memory decline in mild cognitive impairment and healthy aging.
method: 51 older adults (24 with amnestic mild cognitive impairment, 27 healthy controls) completed weekly 8-minute unsupervised online memory assessments for up to 1 year.
Test results were fit to a formal memory consolidation/forgetting model to derive an individualized Seattle-Groningen Memory Assessment (SGMA) score.
Performance was evaluated for reliability, practice effects, stability across materials, and diagnostic discrimination.
evidence_signal: The SGMA score showed mean reliability of r = 0.70, minimal practice effects (about 0.2% increase per assessment), and up to 87% accuracy for detecting mild cognitive impairment.
watch_item: The study is based on a relatively small sample, so broader validation is needed before routine deployment in diverse real-world settings.
paper_title: Detection and Continuous Monitoring of Memory Dysfunction in Mild Cognitive Impairment and Healthy Aging Through Adaptive Computational Phenotyping
